title: Techniques for verifying the accuracy of risk measurement models
venue: Finance and Economics Discussion Series 95-24, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
verification_source: Fed FRASER and EconPapers records, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Introduces the proportion of failures likelihood ratio test for VaR exceptions and discusses its low power on short samples. The Journal of Derivatives version was not checked.

title: Evaluating interval forecasts
verification_source: RePEc IDEAS and EconPapers records, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Defines unconditional coverage, independence and conditional coverage tests for interval forecasts. VaR exceptions are a special case.

title: Coherent measures of risk
authors: Artzner, P., Delbaen, F., Eber, J.-M. and Heath, D.
verification_source: RePEc IDEAS and EconPapers records, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: States the axioms of a coherent risk measure and discusses why quantile based measures such as VaR can fail subadditivity.

title: On the coherence of expected shortfall
verification_source: EconPapers and arXiv records, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Compares definitions of expected shortfall and shows which one is coherent for any loss distribution, including discrete ones.

title: Optimization of conditional value-at-risk
authors: Rockafellar, R. T. and Uryasev, S.
venue: Journal of Risk 2, pp. 21-42 (indexes disagree on the last page)
verification_source: Risk.net, EconPapers and author PDF, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Introduces CVaR minimisation through linear programming. CVaR is the same quantity as ES for continuous losses.

title: Generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity
verification_source: Duke Scholars, RePEc IDEAS, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Defines the GARCH model for time varying variance. This repository uses it to generate synthetic returns with volatility clustering.

title: Elicitability and backtesting: Perspectives for banking regulation
authors: Nolde, N. and Ziegel, J. F.
contribution: Compares traditional backtests with comparative backtests for VaR and ES, and discusses elicitability.

title: Backtesting expected shortfall
verification_source: Existence confirmed through the reference list of Nolde and Ziegel (2017). The article itself was not opened.
contribution: Proposes ES backtest statistics. The Z1 diagnostic in this repository follows the idea in simplified form and is not their full test.

title: Benchmarking state-of-the-art classification algorithms for credit scoring: An update of research
authors: Lessmann, S., Baesens, B., Seow, H.-V. and Thomas, L. C.
verification_source: RePEc IDEAS, dblp and library records, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Large benchmark of 41 classifiers on eight real credit scoring data sets, with several accuracy indicators and a financial impact view.

title: Deep learning for credit scoring: Do or don't?
authors: Gunnarsson, B. R., vanden Broucke, S., Baesens, B., Óskarsdóttir, M. and Lemahieu, W.
verification_source: RePEc IDEAS, dblp and library records, web search 2026-11-25
contribution: Compares deep learning with conventional and ensemble credit scoring methods. The authors conclude deep learning looks inappropriate there and that XGBoost is preferred when classification performance is the main goal.

title: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BCBS d424)
venue: Bank for International Settlements, 7 December 2017, consolidated into the Basel Framework
status: integrated into the consolidated Basel Framework
contribution: Finalises the Basel III reforms, including the revised standardised approach for credit risk.

title: Minimum capital requirements for market risk (BCBS d457)
venue: Bank for International Settlements, 14 January 2019 (rev. February 2019), consolidated into the Basel Framework
status: integrated into the consolidated Basel Framework
contribution: Revised market risk framework. The internal models approach uses expected shortfall, and the standard supersedes the January 2016 version (d352).

title: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments, Section 5.5 Impairment
venue: Effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2018
verification_source: IFRS Foundation illustrative examples page and IASB staff paper, web search 2026-11-25. The link opens the illustrative examples that accompany the standard. Paragraph numbers were not checked.
contribution: Sets the expected credit loss model: 12 month ECL when credit risk has not increased significantly, lifetime ECL after a significant increase, and lifetime ECL for credit impaired assets.

title: Post-implementation Review of IFRS 9 Impairment: summary of feedback and the IASB's responses
authors: IFRS Foundation Trustees, Due Process Oversight Committee staff paper
contribution: Recent official review of how the IFRS 9 impairment model works in practice. Useful for judgement areas such as staging.

title: SR 11-7: Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
authors: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and OCC
contribution: Long standing US guidance on model development, validation and governance. It has been superseded, see SR 26-2.

title: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management
contribution: Current US model risk guidance with a risk based approach. The letter says it is most relevant to organisations above 30 billion dollars in assets and states no effective date.

title: Risk Management and Financial Institutions
venue: Wiley (edition not fixed in this repository)
verification_source: Not verified in the build environment.
contribution: Standard textbook treatment of duration, convexity, VaR, ES and bank regulation.

title: Credit Risk Scorecards: Developing and Implementing Intelligent Credit Scoring
verification_source: Not verified in the build environment.
contribution: Practitioner reference for weight of evidence binning, information value rules of thumb and score scaling.

title: Value at Risk: The New Benchmark for Managing Financial Risk
verification_source: Not verified in the build environment.
contribution: Practitioner reference for historical, parametric and Monte Carlo VaR and for backtesting.
